description: ¡Hola a todos! Somos un equipo de Huancayo que sueña con crear un juego creativo para despertar la imaginación y el gusto por el diseño en las nuevas generaciones, fortaleciendo la inteligencia y el pensamiento creativo a través del conocimiento espacial. Nos mueven la creatividad, la curiosidad y el trabajo en equipo, y te ofrecemos un ambiente cercano y respetuoso donde tu voz importa.
summary: CubeSat Architect is an interactive multiplayer educational game that lets teams of up to four players collaboratively design, build, launch and operate a complete CubeSat mission. Players assume specialized roles (Mission Director, Power & Spacecraft Engineer, Science Officer, Communications Specialist) and must balance real engineering trade-offs: mass, power, budget, data volume, communications capacity, orbital constraints and scientific return.The game features three progressive mission scenarios: Andean glacier monitoring from polar LEO, lunar ice and magnetic field mapping in low lunar orbit, and solar weather observation from the Sun-Earth L1 point. Players select spacecraft structure, solar arrays, batteries, attitude control, thermal protection, propulsion, scientific instruments and launch vehicles. Every decision has clear consequences on system performance.A free sandbox mode allows unrestricted experimentation, while the multiplayer mode forces negotiation and teamwork under resource limits. Real NASA data concepts and CubeSat design principles are embedded throughout the experience. The pixel-art interface makes complex systems engineering accessible and engaging for students and enthusiasts.By simulating the full mission lifecycle—from concept to operations—CubeSat Architect turns abstract engineering trade-offs into a hands-on, collaborative learning experience that directly addresses the challenge of teaching integrated space mission design.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
CubeSat Architect is a real-time collaborative web game. Players join a room, choose one of four roles, select a scientific mission, configure every major CubeSat subsystem (structure, power, ADCS, propulsion, thermal, payload, communications) and choose a compatible launcher. During the operations phase they must manage power, pointing and data downlink while dealing with anomalies. Success depends on both technical decisions and team coordination.

What are the benefits and impact?
The game makes the complex, multi-disciplinary nature of space mission design tangible. Students experience first-hand how adding a better instrument increases mass, power demand and data volume, and how those changes affect the launcher and overall mission success. It trains systems thinking, negotiation and prioritization—skills that are difficult to teach through traditional lectures.

What tools and technologies were used?
React, TypeScript, HTML5 Canvas (pixel-art rendering), real-time multiplayer (WebSockets), and Tailwind CSS. The interface deliberately uses a retro pixel-art style to lower the entry barrier while keeping the engineering content rigorous.

Why is it creative and innovative?
Most educational space tools focus on a single subsystem (orbit, rocket, or spacecraft). CubeSat Architect is one of the few that forces players to manage the full end-to-end mission as a system, with explicit role-based collaboration and progressive mission difficulty. The combination of serious engineering constraints with an approachable, game-like interface is its main innovation.
projectRefs: Exploring team dynamics and performance in extended space missions using agent-based modeling
